bill_of_materials.why: Three failures, three separate arguments - not one argument with two failures appended to it. (a) F3: all four probe runs computed the per-slice Wilson interval correctly and then set the reporting floor with a round number of their own invention - 30, 200 and 350, three different floors from identical data. The gap is not arithmetic, it is that the cut has no origin, and an instruction saying 'cite a measured interval' with no interval in reach only moves the invention one step. C1's measured half-widths are what a step can point AT; C2 and C3 are the two ways that pointing goes wrong (a naive interval that ignores clustering, and a round number whose author calls its parameters fictional). (b) F1 has a DIFFERENT mechanism and needs the file for a different reason. The three runs that stopped at exact-match dedup were not inventing anything - they were confident their detector had finished. What they lacked was a measurement of what a verbatim detector cannot see, and C6 is exactly that measurement: F1 0.816-0.926 on verbatim duplicates and 0.0 on every rephrased one. The body can assert 'exact match is not enough' in one line; what it cannot carry is the evidence that makes an analyst distrust a clean dedup report. C5 supplies the size of the consequence with a number - Transformer-XL scores 10.11 perplexity on the duplicated subset against 23.58 on the unique one, with the limit that the metric is perplexity and so gives no conversion into accuracy points - and C4 supplies that it happens in real held-out sets at 4.6 percent of the C4 validation set and 14.4 percent of RealNews, with the limit that this is whole-example similarity and does not transfer to a curated production set. Both are load-bearing rather than decorative: without C5 the step is a rule with no consequence attached, and without C4 it is a laboratory result with no claim on anyone's actual data. (c) F2's mechanism is a third one again: the runs that shipped a 'held-out pool, also usable as a dev set' were not wrong about anything checkable, and there is no single number that settles them. C10, C11 and C12 are bundled BECAUSE they disagree - which is the reason the body's step 3 asks the reader to name a regime rather than to obey a rule. A body cannot carry a live disagreement in one line without flattening it into whichever side it quotes. HOW THE CONTESTED MATERIAL IS MARKED, since bundling it in the same citable voice as the settled material would let a future invocation quote C10 as established: section 4 of the file is headed 'two bodies of evidence that do not agree', opens with 'This disagreement is NOT resolved, and a step that cites one side must name which regime it assumes', is laid out as Side A and Side B, and every claim on both sides carries its own 'Does not establish' paragraph - C10's says it is a worst case by construction giving no safe reuse count, C12's says Kaggle measures a PROTECTED regime. The file's table of contents marks section 4 UNRESOLVED, C3 DERIVED and C7 REPEATED. Kept OUT of SKILL.md: thirteen quotes with locators and limits is 200-plus lines loaded on every invocation whether or not a number is in question, and figures this specific go stale. REACHABILITY, added at revision 4 after an independent pointer reader found C2 justified here and cited by no step: four parts of this file are deliberately NOT reachable from a step and the file now says so in its own contents. C2 is bundled and uncited because its limits exclude the population this method is about ('not established for production-log data at all') - a step citing it would breach its limit, and dropping it would leave the reader with C1's narrowest-case intervals and no warning that they are narrowest-case, which step 2 now states in its own words without citing C2 as evidence. C7 and section 3 (C8, C9, C13) support the four behaviours the skill declines to teach because the baseline already does them - they are a lookup surface for someone checking WHY, not step support. Section 6 is UNQUOTED and nothing may be cited from it.

The output shape, as headings and fields with nothing filled in. Each observed failure gets a structural home and the mapping is named here so it can be checked. F1 -> 'Near-duplicates', whose fields are the detector used, the threshold AND HOW IT WAS CHOSEN, and the cluster count and distinct-string count as two separate rows, because 3 of 4 probe runs conflated them. F2 -> 'Holdout', which carries the look log as a table with a date and a reason per row under a Sealed field. F3 -> 'Per-slice sizing'. NOTE, corrected at revision 5: this entry used to say the columns were n, the interval at that n, and the SOURCE of the floor. The artefact abandoned that mechanism during the steps rounds - SKILL.md now says in as many words that 'a source column is not enough either' and the Rules say 'a citation is not a tolerance' - and the asset has no source column. The columns are a gated decision, a tolerance, the inversion's inputs including p and when p was fixed, an owner and a date, and then n pre-collapse, n post-collapse, the interval and the floor. A NOTED ASYMMETRY, raised by the 4.0 reader and accepted rather than argued away: F3's countermeasure works because C1 gives a real number to cite, and F2's does not have an equivalent anchor - a template cannot stop a plausible row being written into a look log. What the F2 section can do, and does, is make the WEAKER claim visible: the Sealed field must read UNSEALED when nothing seals it, and an empty log under UNSEALED is the record saying there is no holdout. That is a smaller countermeasure than F3's and it is recorded as smaller. C10 is the nearest thing F2 has to an anchor and step 3 cites it, but it is a synthetic worst case and cannot carry the weight C1 carries.

package.verifiable is true, so eval.exists makes this an error if absent. Five evals. Four of them ARE the four prompts the 6.1 arms run, so nothing in this bundle is a scenario that was never executed - the exact defect the incumbent's evals.md carries (11 scenarios, every result produced by predicting what a run would do). The fifth is the negative trigger, scored at 6.5 by triggers.py. Mapping: E1 (pick the 200) carries F1 and the stratification-with-a-floor half of F3; E3 (what must be removed) carries F1 alone and is the sharper of the two because 3 of 4 runs failed it identically; E4 (how many per slice) carries F3. E2 (is 88.75 trustworthy) is a DELIBERATE, BOUNDED EXCEPTION to this bill's own rule that a bundled item answers an observed failure: it answers an observed NON-failure. The baseline passes it 4 of 4 and it is here so that a skill which teaches three new behaviours cannot quietly lose a fourth that already worked. It is the only such exception in this bundle and evals.json labels it as one in its own text. F2 has no eval at 6.1. This is a decision with a SCHEDULED RECKONING, not a disclosure left to persist: two reasons (the probe's F2 evidence is weak on 2 of the SAME 3 runs that failed F2 - the three are probe.A.without.r2, which produced a heldout_pool described as usable as a dev set, and probe.B.without.r1 and probe.B.without.r2, which produced no split at all; those last two are the weak pair, because their task set never asked for one, so the honest count is one clear F2 failure and two runs that were never given the chance to fail it, and an eval that asks 'seal the holdout' telegraphs its answer), and two named places it is revisited - phase 7.2 triage must state whether F2 went untested, and phase 6.6 field_trial is where a genuinely reused holdout could be observed. If neither happens the build report names F2 as unmeasured, and that sentence is the reckoning.

2000 rows with known ground truth: four slices at 82.35 / 13.2 / 3.35 / 1.1 percent, per-slice accuracy 0.947 / 0.670 / 0.463 / 0.318, 6 near-duplicate template clusters covering 120 rows that collapse to 60 distinct strings, and 37 rows flagged in the in_fewshot_prompt column. Referenced from evals.json files[], which eval.files-resolve requires to resolve under the skill root. KNOWN DEFECT, AND ITS EFFECT ON THE EVALS ASSESSED RATHER THAN MERELY DISCLOSED: 1880 of the 2000 rows carry placeholder query text containing its own slice label, which all four probe runs found. CORRECTED AT REVISION 5 - the first assessment of this defect was wrong and the whole-artefact reviewer found it. The placeholder rows are themselves a templated family by this skill's own step 1, whose normalisation clause collapses them to four strings; measured over the whole file, normalising 8-hex tokens and digits leaves 64 distinct strings, of which 4 cover the 1880 placeholder rows. So a run applying step 1 CORRECTLY reports about 10 families, not the package's 6, and would be graded as a miss for being right. The defect does not make the evals easier - it makes the supplied ground truth wrong for them. evals.json now carries the corrected structure and the expectation set at 6.2 is written against it. Original, now-superseded assessment: it does NOT inflate E1, E3 or E4. The slice column is supplied explicitly in the CSV, so a slice label inside the query string adds no information a run did not already have; and the entire near-duplicate structure the F1 evals turn on lives in the 120 real-text rows, which are unaffected. It WOULD matter to any eval that ran a model on these queries and scored its answers, and none of these five does. Not repaired here, because repairing it would change what the probe measured; carried to 7.2 as a test bug.

Added at 8.2, and the addition is a finding rather than an oversight. The house rule is that a talent is not shipped until SPECIFIC tests are authored and PASS, persisted as evals.md - and the bill of materials written at 4.0 planned evals/evals.json and never planned the report that rule requires. The artefact checker caught it as 'present but unplanned' the moment the file appeared. It carries the executed result: three arms x two repeats x two blind graders, the per-scenario table, the routing outcome, and the reason the verdict is iterate. Its most important section is the last one, which says what these evals do NOT test - F2 has no eval of its own, nothing ran on a real instance, and the grader was never calibrated against a planted defect.

not_bundled.why: Not planned at 4.0. The contract's content_source for scripts is DISCOVERED from the eval transcripts - a helper is bundled only if independent runs wrote the same one. There is already a signal: probe.A.without.r1 and probe.B.without.r2 each independently wrote a curate.py. Phase 7.1 decides it from the 6.1 transcripts; if it says yes, this bill of materials is amended there and the amendment is an event.

not_bundled.what: a second reference for the incumbent's own material
not_bundled.why: The incumbent SKILL.md is 161 lines with 0 references and 0 URLs. Its steps are being carried forward where the probe showed the baseline needs them, and dropped where the probe showed it does not. It is evidence about SCOPE and VOCABULARY, not about the world, so it does not become a reference file - it has nothing to cite.
